concepts.name: Variables and values
concepts.description: A name refers to a value; assignment changes what a name refers to.

concepts.name: Evaluating expressions
concepts.description: Arithmetic and comparison expressions such as n - 1 and n == 0 produce values.

concepts.name: Conditionals
concepts.description: if statements choose which code runs based on a boolean expression.

concepts.name: Defining and calling functions
concepts.description: A function is defined once and can be called many times.

concepts.name: Parameters and arguments
concepts.description: A call passes argument values into the function's parameters; each call gets its own parameter values.

concepts.name: Return values
concepts.description: return ends the call and hands a value back to the caller.

concepts.name: Execution flow of calls
concepts.description: When a function is called, execution moves into it, then resumes after the call when it returns.

concepts.name: The call stack
concepts.description: Active calls are kept in a stack; the most recent call finishes first.

concepts.name: A function calling itself
concepts.description: A recursive call is an ordinary call whose target happens to be the same function, with its own parameter values.

concepts.name: Base case
concepts.description: The condition under which the function stops calling itself.

concepts.name: Recursive step and progress
concepts.description: Each recursive call must move the arguments closer to the base case.

concepts.name: Tracing recursive execution
concepts.description: Predict output and order of calls and returns for a recursive function.

concepts.name: Returning values through recursive calls
concepts.description: A recursive call's returned value is used by the caller, for example n * factorial(n - 1).

concepts.name: Writing a simple recursive function
concepts.description: Identify the base case and recursive step for a small problem and write the function.

learningObjective: Understand recursive execution and write simple recursive functions.

sources.text:
sys.setrecursionlimit(limit)
Set the maximum depth of the Python interpreter stack to limit. This limit prevents infinite recursion from causing an overflow of the C stack and crashing Python.

sources.title: Recursion (computer science) - Wikipedia
sources.text: In computer science, recursion is a method of solving a computational problem where the solution depends on solutions to smaller instances of the same problem.

sources.title: Tail call - Wikipedia
sources.text: In computer science, a tail call is a subroutine call performed as the final action of a procedure. If the target of a tail call is the same subroutine, the subroutine is said to be tail recursive, which is a special case of direct recursion. Tail recursion (or tail-end recursion) is particularly useful, and is often easy to optimize in implementations. Tail calls can be implemented without adding a new stack frame to the call stack. Most of the frame of the current procedure is no longer needed, and can be replaced by the frame of the tail call, modified as appropriate (similar to overlay for processes, but for function calls). The program can then jump to the called subroutine. Producing such code instead of a standard call sequence is called tail-call elimination or tail-call optimization.

Check rules: serve 3 questions, one per tier (1, 2, 3). Pick one from each tier at random, never reuse a question the session has already seen. Tier 3 is the transfer question. At least one question must have requiresWhy = true (tier 2).
